sentence: This project tests whether air samplers in schools can measure and forecast the spread of respiratory viruses, and uses viral sequencing to find variants.
This project builds probes from bioluminescent and fluorescent proteins that record calcium signaling in living T cells.
This project develops a gene therapy that uses an RNA-targeting CRISPR tool to silence mutant superoxide dismutase 1 in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.
This project uses fruit flies to study how gene expression varies and how transcription factors shape new genes and new expression.
This project combines mutagenesis screens, biophysical assays and deep learning models to study how protein disorder evolves rapidly, using fertilization as a model.
This project collects and stores biopsies and runs first tests on the tissue using immunohistochemistry and sequencing.
This project studies the eye and visual pathways, including visual perception, visual circuitry and retinal degeneration.
This project uses Vaccinia virus to find protein interfaces that form when viruses assemble inside the infected cell.
This project studies how a translational regulator controls stress responses, morphogenesis and virulence properties of the fungus Candida albicans.
This project studies malaria and diseases spread by mosquitoes and ticks, including how pathogens cause disease and spread through mosquito vectors.
This project tests whether a gene therapy given by a single intravenous injection is safe and works for a rare neuromuscular disorder.
This project uses imaging mass spectrometry to study metabolomic changes in brain cells during aging and neurodegeneration.
This project studies how cells with DNA damage survive and grow as tissues renew, and how this relates to cancer development.
This project builds a sequencing method to map abasic sites in DNA and studies how toxicant exposure affects their repair.
This project develops a simplified and rapid method that uses CRISPR-Cas12 to detect DNA sequences specific to Leishmania species.
This project labels vesicles from stem cells and tests whether MRI can track them in mouse models of multiple sclerosis or amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.
This project tests whether a cell growth supplement derived from an immortal cancer cell line can support cell proliferation as well as widely used supplements.
This project studies how clonal hematopoiesis develops and how the niche can control it.
This project creates genetic stocks of the nematode with fluorescently tagged secreted proteins to show where they are expressed and localized.
This project tests combining oncolytic reoviruses, immune checkpoint inhibitors and targeted internal radiation therapy delivered into the bladder to treat non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer.
